title: Ironline Forge challenge-coin program: neutralize six differently-lit reference sheets to one common white point, trace the crest and five coin faces into a weight-matched vector family with full-detail and single-strike versions, author two struck-metal proofs of the crest, and cut out the finished sample coin as a webshop packshot
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork logo + challenge-coin vectorization brief (cand_38, db_i 95): the client already HAS hand-mocked concept art and needs it turned into polished, true vector artwork for a primary crest plus several symbolic coin-face designs, coin-ready and readable at small sizes, with versions that reproduce in flat black, reversed white, and struck gold and silver metal, deliverable as clean scalable vector plus product-ready exports for a mint/manufacturer handoff. The real client is laundered to the fictional heavy-industry crew brand 'Ironline Forge' running an internal challenge-coin program; no real company, product, unit insignia, marketplace, or design software is named anywhere. REASONABLY ENRICHED into a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark AND repaired against the audit: the prior version was flagged (group G5) because it minted the black/white/gold/silver 'variants' with image_fill_area (which solid-fills the whole mask and turns a detailed emblem into a black BLOB, destroying every interior counter) and image_apply_color_overlay (a whole-image, opacity-free tint that cannot make a clean masked recolor), and it shipped a 'white #FFFFFF variant' that no connector step actually produced plus a 2000x2000 canvas no crop step established. Those defective outputs are removed entirely. In their place the client is modeled as supplying SIX flat reference sheets - the primary crest lockup plus five coin-face emblems - each hand-mocked and photographed/scanned on a DIFFERENT day under DIFFERENT shop lighting (so they do NOT match out of camera) and each carrying a small in-frame 18% grey calibration card and corner registration ticks in the margin, PLUS a seventh image that is a photograph of one physically STRUCK sample coin (real metal, relief, sheen, on felt) that looks like 'just another coin image' but is a photo of a 3D object and must not be traced. The differently-lit sheets and their in-frame grey cards turn cross-family stroke-weight consistency into a trippable craft target rather than an assertion; the black/white/gold/silver requirement is honored as a reproduction quality of a single clean vector master (flat-black positive and reversed-white knockout are properties of the same paths) plus two agent-AUTHORED struck-metal proofs of the crest built from tone/tint/grain primitives - not four solid-fill blobs. No measurement is asked of the agent: it neutralizes each grey card BY EYE and REPORTS the parameters it dialed; the white-point tolerance is the grader's acceptance rubric on the retained card-bearing masters, not a step the agent performs.
one_line_ask: Rebuild Ironline Forge's crest and five coin-face concepts as one weight-matched production vector family: neutralize each differently-lit reference sheet to a common white point by eye using its in-frame grey card, trace each into a full-detail multi-shape vector and a single-color strike master, author warm-metal and cool-metal struck proofs of the crest, and cut out the photographed sample coin as a webshop packshot without tracing it.
full_brief:
Ironline Forge runs an internal challenge-coin program and we finally want it done properly. We have rough hand-mocked concept art for our primary crest and for five coin faces, and we need it all rebuilt as clean, true vector artwork that scales to any size, holds up at coin scale, and can go to a mint. Fair warning up front: the reference art was mocked up and captured on different days in different corners of the shop, so the sheets do NOT match - some are warmer, some cooler, some brighter or dimmer, and a couple are a little crooked. Every sheet has a small grey calibration card and a few registration ticks printed in the bottom margin so you can get the paper reading as one true, identical neutral white across the whole set before you build anything. This matters: if the sheets get cleaned to different whites, the marks will rebuild at different line weights and the family will look like it was drawn by different people - and on a coin next to each other that is obvious and unacceptable. The crest and the five coins have to read as ONE set, same visual weight, same proportion.

What we need back per mark: a full-detail vector that keeps the emblem's raised fill and its fine keyline as separate shapes (so the mint can strike it in more than one level), AND a single-color strike master - one solid silhouette - for a single-level die or a laser cut. The whole family has to reproduce cleanly as flat black line art and as a reversed white knockout for dark backgrounds, and it has to look right struck in metal. For the crest specifically, show us two finished metal proofs so we can sign off on the look: one warm (gold / antique bronze) and one cool (brushed silver / nickel), each reading like a real struck coin, not a flat color swatch. Make those proofs your call on the finish - that sign-off image is the thing we are buying your eye for.

One more file: alongside the reference art we are sending a photograph of one physically struck sample coin from an earlier small run - real metal on a felt tray. That one is a photo of a finished object, not reference art; we need it as a clean product cut-out on white for the webshop at 1600x2000, and it should NOT end up in the vector set. Finally, hand back a short sheet listing, per reference, the straighten angle and the white-balance and tone moves you settled on, so we can trust the set really was matched to one target instead of each fixed on its own. The vectors must be original artwork rebuilt from our supplied concepts - not lifted from any existing font or clip file.

inputs.name: crest_master_sheet.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked concept sheet for a heavy-industry crew crest: a bold heraldic shield containing a stylized piston-and-gear motif with a compact condensed-sans wordmark reading 'IRONLINE FORGE' on a banner beneath it, rendered as a single deep gunmetal ink with a thin secondary keyline outline on white paper. In the bottom margin print a small neutral 18% grey calibration square and four black corner registration ticks. The capture is slightly COOL and a touch dim (mild blue-grey cast, white paper reading about 234 not 255), lit unevenly so the upper-left is brighter, faint offset-print texture in the flat ink, and the whole sheet rotated about +2.4 degrees clockwise so the banner baseline is not level. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI gloss, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable source and the HERO that establishes the house white point. It is deliberately COOL, dim and tilted +2.4deg: the agent must dial its own straighten angle plus its own warming/whites moves to neutralize the in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE (never reading a pixel) and report what it dialed. Two-tone (gunmetal fill + thin keyline) so the full-detail whole-raster trace keeps fill and keyline as SEPARATE closed shapes while the isolate-then-trace path collapses them to ONE silhouette strike master. The wordmark's enclosed letter counters are why the metal proofs are rendered on the whole cleaned plate (a struck-disc look) rather than a background knockout - image_remove_background cannot punch enclosed interior counters, so no counter-knockout is claimed. Its lighting/tilt deliberately do NOT match the coin sheets, so a single shared cleanup recipe fails.

inputs.name: coin_ref_raptor.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked challenge-coin face concept: a symbolic spread-winged raptor gripping a spanner and a lightning bolt in a circular emblem, a single dark ink fill with a fine keyline and a small micro-text banner, on white paper with a small 18% grey calibration square and four corner registration ticks in the bottom margin. This capture is WARMER and BRIGHTER than the crest sheet (mild amber cast, white paper reading about 250, slightly hot in the lower-right), faint offset texture, and the sheet rotated about -3.6 degrees counter-clockwise. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable coin source, deliberately MISMATCHED to the crest: warmer, brighter, tilted the OPPOSITE way (-3.6deg vs +2.4deg). The agent neutralizes its grey card to the SAME white point as the crest but with its own opposite-sign moves; reusing the crest's numbers here leaves it off-neutral and the raptor traces at a heavier line weight than the crest - the mismatch is invisible until the two SVGs sit side by side. The micro-text banner stresses 'readable at small sizes'. Same nominal line weight and proportion as the other coins once cleaned correctly.

inputs.name: coin_ref_gearglobe.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked challenge-coin face concept: a globe wrapped by a mechanical gear ring with two crossed mallets behind it, concentric circular emblem, single dark ink with a fine keyline, on white paper with a small 18% grey calibration square and four corner registration ticks in the bottom margin. This capture has a distinct GREEN fluorescent cast and is evenly but flatly lit (white paper reading about 242), faint offset texture, shot square with negligible tilt. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable coin source under a GREEN fluorescent cast - a third, different neutralization direction (pull green/magenta balance, not just warm/cool) that no warm-or-cool recipe copied from the crest or raptor will fix. Shot flat, so no straighten step is needed for this one - the agent must recognize that and not invent a rotation. The concentric gear teeth are fine internal geometry that only survives if the plate is cleaned crisply before tracing.

inputs.name: coin_ref_anvil.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked challenge-coin face concept: a heavy anvil with a forging hammer crossed over it inside a rope-border ring, bold symbolic emblem, single dark ink with a fine keyline, on white paper with a small 18% grey calibration square and four corner registration ticks in the bottom margin. This capture is WARM amber and slightly dim (white paper reading about 236), faint offset texture, shot square with negligible tilt. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable coin source, warm-and-dim - close in cast to the raptor but at a different brightness, so its own correction is again distinct (warm the opposite direction but lift the paper more than the raptor needs). Shot flat: no straighten. The repeating rope-border ring is fine repeating geometry that a naive un-cleaned trace turns into broken beads.

inputs.name: coin_ref_reaper.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked challenge-coin face concept: a side-profile harvester/tractor silhouette inside a wheat-wreath circular border with a small star at the top, symbolic single-ink emblem with a fine keyline, on white paper with a small 18% grey calibration square and four corner registration ticks in the bottom margin. This capture is clearly COOL daylight (blue cast) and bright (white paper reading about 248), faint offset texture, and the sheet rotated about +3.1 degrees clockwise. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable coin source, cool-and-bright and tilted +3.1deg - ties the agriculture vertical into the set and needs a WARM-toward-neutral move plus a downward brightness pull, opposite in sign to the warm coins, plus its own straighten angle (different from the crest's and the raptor's). The wheat-wreath is dense fine detail that only traces cleanly off a correctly neutralized plate.

inputs.name: coin_ref_piston.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down scan of a hand-mocked challenge-coin face concept: a single piston with a lightning bolt behind it flanked by a laurel half-wreath, symbolic single-ink emblem with a fine keyline, on white paper with a small 18% grey calibration square and four corner registration ticks in the bottom margin. This capture has a faint MAGENTA mixed-light cast and is medium brightness (white paper reading about 240), faint offset texture, shot square with negligible tilt. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI, flat art, 2600x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable coin source under a MAGENTA cast - yet another distinct neutralization direction (add green / pull magenta), different again from the green gearglobe and from the warm/cool frames. Shot flat: no straighten. Rebuilding all six grey cards to one shared neutral white is only possible if each frame is diagnosed and corrected on its own; a single global white balance across the set cannot land six different casts on one white point.

inputs.name: sample_strike_photo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a single physically struck metal challenge coin lying on a dark grey felt tray, shot slightly from above. The coin is antique bronze with raised relief of an industrial emblem, real specular glints on the raised edges, soft shadowing in the recesses, fine machining marks and a knurled rim, a shallow contact shadow on the felt. The coin is the clear centered subject. Documentary catalog realism, real metal, no CGI gloss, 3600x4500.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY at camera scale (3600x4500). It looks like 'a sixth coin design' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of a struck 3D metal object with relief, specular sheen and machining marks on felt - it CANNOT be traced into clean vector (the sheen, recesses and rim would become garbage relief paths). Its only correct use is the webshop packshot: knock the felt ground to transparency with image_remove_background, then downscale/reframe to the 1600x2000 product tile (a pure downscale from the 3600x4500 source - never an upscale or canvas extend). A naive agent that runs it through the same clean->trace spine it just used on the six flat sheets - or that reads the brief's 'vector every coin design' too literally - produces an unusable trace; the failure is only visible in the SVG path data. Carries NO grey card because it is never neutralized or traced.

outputs.name: crest_relief_art.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the primary crest: the gunmetal emblem fill and the fine keyline preserved as SEPARATE closed shapes (for multi-level striking), transparent ground, tight continuous paths. Traced by image_vectorize from the straightened, grey-neutralized, cropped crest plate; line weight matched to the coin family because every sheet was driven to a common white point first. Reproduces cleanly as flat-black positive and as a reversed-white knockout (same paths, inverted fill) and readable at coin scale.

outputs.name: crest_strike_mask.svg
outputs.spec: Single-color strike master of the crest: one solid silhouette (fill + keyline collapsed to one shape) for a single-level die or laser cut. Produced by feeding the crest emblem selection to image_vectorize, which returns a black silhouette - deliberately the opposite polarity to crest_relief_art.svg.

outputs.name: crest_proof_bronze.png
outputs.spec: Agent-AUTHORED warm-metal struck proof of the crest for client sign-off: the cleaned crest plate rendered as an antique-bronze struck coin, built from primitives (tone/contrast shaped for a raised-relief read, a warm monochromatic metal tint, and a fine cast-metal grain) - reads like real struck metal, not a flat color swatch. The finish is the agent's aesthetic decision.

outputs.name: crest_proof_nickel.png
outputs.spec: Agent-AUTHORED cool-metal struck proof of the crest: the same relief-shaped base rendered as brushed nickel/silver via a neutral monochromatic metal tint, matched in relief read to the bronze proof so the client can compare warm vs cool finishes of one master.

outputs.name: coin_raptor.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the raptor coin face traced from its background-neutralized, cropped plate; keyline and fill as separate shapes, line weight matched to the crest and the rest of the coin family because both sheets were neutralized to the common white point before tracing.

outputs.name: coin_gearglobe.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the gear-globe coin face; concentric gear teeth held crisp because the green-cast plate was neutralized and cropped tight before tracing. Weight-matched to the family.

outputs.name: coin_anvil.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the anvil coin face; the repeating rope-border ring traced clean off a correctly neutralized plate. Weight-matched to the family.

outputs.name: coin_reaper.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the harvester/wheat-wreath coin face traced from its straightened, warmed-to-neutral, cropped plate. Weight-matched to the family.

outputs.name: coin_piston.svg
outputs.spec: Full-detail vector of the piston/laurel coin face traced from its magenta-neutralized, cropped plate. Weight-matched to the family, completing the crest + five-coin set.

outputs.name: sample_packshot_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Webshop product cut-out of the finished sample coin: the felt ground knocked out with image_remove_background and the subject reframed/downscaled to exactly 1600x2000 on white, sRGB. A RASTER packshot with NO vector paths - this file proves the sample photo was correctly triaged as a photograph and kept OUT of the vector set.

outputs.name: applied_settings_log.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the six reference sheets, the straighten angle used (or 'none' for the flat scans), and the white-balance temperature/tint plus exposure/whites it dialed to land that sheet's grey card on the shared neutral white point. This is the acceptance artifact that makes 'the set was matched to one target' checkable - the six corrections must be NON-identical (six different casts) while converging on one white point.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: crest_master_sheet.png, coin_ref_raptor.png, coin_ref_gearglobe.png, coin_ref_anvil.png, coin_ref_reaper.png, coin_ref_piston.png, sample_strike_photo.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Single ingest: bring the six flat reference sheets and the finished sample-coin photo into Creative Cloud storage. Every later step consumes a named prior output; this is the only upload. Plumbing, not the difficulty.
CREST BRANCH. Level the crest sheet so the banner baseline is square before anything else, and report the correcting angle. Coins mint on a true axis, so the trace must inherit no tilt.

Neutralize this sheet's in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE: dial temperature/tint and whites/exposure until the grey card looks truly neutral and the paper reads as a clean white, killing any cast and the offset texture. This sheet's settled white point IS the shared target the other five must hit. The agent never reads a pixel value; it judges by eye and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure/whites it dialed. Retain this card-bearing neutralized master for grading.
Crop tight to the crest artwork, dropping the bottom-margin grey card, registration ticks and surplus paper so the trace sees only the mark on clean white. Report the crop bounds.

DELIVERABLE (full-detail crest): whole-raster trace of the cleaned crest so the gunmetal fill and the fine keyline come through as separate closed shapes for multi-level striking. No selection - this is the multi-shape polarity.
Select 'the crest emblem and lettering' on the cleaned crest plate to isolate the combined mark from the white ground - the input for the single-color strike master.

DELIVERABLE (single-strike master): vectorize the SELECTION, which returns one solid silhouette (fill+keyline collapsed) for a single-level die or laser cut. Same cleaned plate as step 5, deliberately the DIFFERENT vectorize polarity (selection->silhouette vs whole-raster multi-shape). Swap the two and the full-detail art loses its keyline or the strike master arrives as un-cuttable two-shape art.

METAL-PROOF BRANCH. On the cleaned crest plate, shape tone and contrast so the emblem reads as raised relief on a struck disc (deepen the recessed tones, hold an edge highlight) - the neutral base both metal proofs share. Authored by eye from adjustment primitives, not a preset.
Render the relief base as a warm antique-bronze metal via a single warm monochromatic tint (whole-image tint, honest use). The agent chooses the bronze hue and depth.

DELIVERABLE (warm-metal sign-off proof): add a fine cast-metal grain so the bronze reads like struck metal rather than a flat swatch. This authored finish is the client's sign-off image and the agent's aesthetic call.

DELIVERABLE (cool-metal sign-off proof): render the SAME relief base as brushed nickel/silver via a neutral monochromatic tint, matched in relief read to the bronze proof so the client compares warm vs cool finishes of one master. Reuses the step-8 base, so the two proofs are the same coin in two metals.
RAPTOR COIN BRANCH (re-consumes uploaded_assets). Level this sheet's tilt and report the angle - a different angle and direction than the crest needed.

Neutralize this sheet's in-frame grey card BY EYE to the SAME shared white point set on the crest, using this frame's own moves; judge the card until it looks neutral and the paper matches the crest's white. Never read a pixel; REPORT the temperature/tint/exposure/whites you dialed. Retain this card-bearing master for grading.
Crop tight to the coin face, dropping the grey card, ticks and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.

DELIVERABLE: full-detail whole-raster trace of the cleaned raptor plate, keyline and fill as separate shapes. Because this sheet was driven to the same white point as the crest, it traces at the same line weight.

GEAR-GLOBE COIN BRANCH. This scan is flat (no tilt), so no straighten - go straight to neutralizing its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point with this frame's own balance move, and REPORT the settings dialed. Retain the card-bearing master for grading.
Crop tight to the coin face, dropping card, ticks and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.
DELIVERABLE: full-detail trace of the gear-globe; the concentric gear teeth hold because the plate was neutralized and cropped tight first. Weight-matched to the family.

ANVIL COIN BRANCH. Flat scan (no tilt): neutralize its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point with this frame's own move, and REPORT the settings. Retain the card-bearing master for grading.
Crop tight to the coin face, dropping card, ticks and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.
DELIVERABLE: full-detail trace of the anvil; the repeating rope-border ring stays crisp off the cleaned plate. Weight-matched to the family.
HARVESTER COIN BRANCH. Level this sheet's tilt and report the angle (different again from the crest and raptor).
Neutralize this sheet's in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point with this frame's own balance move, and REPORT the settings dialed. Retain the card-bearing master for grading.
Crop tight to the coin face, dropping card, ticks and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.
DELIVERABLE: full-detail trace of the harvester/wheat-wreath coin off its straightened, neutralized plate. Weight-matched to the family.

PISTON COIN BRANCH. Flat scan (no tilt): neutralize its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point with this frame's own balance move, and REPORT the settings. Retain the card-bearing master for grading.
Crop tight to the coin face, dropping card, ticks and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.
DELIVERABLE: full-detail trace of the piston/laurel coin off its neutralized plate, completing the crest + five-coin family. Weight-matched to the set.

SAMPLE-COIN BRANCH: knock the felt tray ground of the finished sample-coin photo to transparency, isolating the coin as a clean product cut-out. This is the correct treatment for a photographed 3D object - it is NOT sent to the tracer.

DELIVERABLE (webshop packshot): subject-aware reframe + downscale of the sample-coin cut-out to exactly 1600x2000 on white, sRGB. A pure downscale from the 3600x4500 source - never canvas-extend, never upscale. A raster deliverable with no vector paths.

chaining_note: Single ingest at step 1 (uploaded_assets); every later step consumes a named prior output. CREST BRANCH forks from uploaded_assets: auto_straighten(2)->apply_adjustments(3, neutralize the crest grey card by eye = the SHARED white-point target)->crop_to_bounds(4); the cleaned plate crest_cropped(4) is a reuse hub with THREE consumers - whole-raster trace(5)=crest_relief_art.svg (multi-shape), select_by_prompt(6)->vectorize the selection(7)=crest_strike_mask.svg (single silhouette), and apply_adjustments(8)=crest_relief_base which feeds two AUTHORED metal proofs: monochromatic_tint(9)->add_grain(10)=crest_proof_bronze.png and monochromatic_tint(11)=crest_proof_nickel.png (both off the same step-8 base, so they are one coin in two metals). Five COIN BRANCHES each re-consume uploaded_assets and each reason a DIFFERENT correction to the SAME white point before a full-detail trace: raptor auto_straighten(12)->neutralize(13)->crop(14)->trace(15); gearglobe neutralize(16, flat scan so no straighten)->crop(17)->trace(18); anvil neutralize(19, flat)->crop(20)->trace(21); reaper auto_straighten(22)->neutralize(23)->crop(24)->trace(25); piston neutralize(26, flat)->crop(27)->trace(28). SAMPLE-COIN BRANCH takes the photograph down a deliberately different path: remove_background(29) knocks the felt ground to transparency (NOT a trace) and crop_and_resize(30) downscales/reframes to the 1600x2000 packshot. Nine SVGs+one strike master, two authored metal proofs, one raster packshot and the applied-settings log all emerge from the chain; no image_fill_area, no image_apply_color_overlay, no ZIP, no per-record layout export.
difficulty_rationale: Depth, not breadth: 30 dependent connector calls across 10 distinct Adobe tools, but the difficulty is in the per-frame reasoning, not the count. The agent must (a) recognize the six reference sheets are lit under SIX different casts (cool, warm, green-fluorescent, warm-dim, cool-daylight, magenta) and tilted differently (three tilted, three flat), and therefore choose per-sheet straighten angles AND per-sheet white-balance/tone moves that all converge on ONE shared white point read off each frame's in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE - a single global balance across the set cannot land six different casts on one white, and a mismatch traces the family at different line weights; (b) use image_vectorize two different ways on the crest - a whole-raster trace that keeps fill and keyline as separate shapes (multi-level strike art) versus a selection->silhouette trace for the single-level strike master; (c) AUTHOR two struck-metal proofs of the crest from primitives (relief-shaped tone, warm vs neutral monochromatic tint, cast grain) rather than dropping a flat color fill; (d) triage the photographed sample coin as non-traceable and route it to remove_background + downscale instead of the tracer it just used on the six flat sheets; and (e) keep prep-before-trace discipline (straighten where needed, neutralize, crop to bounds) so every trace inherits neither tilt, cast, nor offset texture. It respects every connector limit: image_vectorize is the only raster->vector path; the black/white/gold/silver requirement is honored as reproduction properties of one clean vector master (flat-black positive, reversed-white knockout) plus two authored metal proofs, NOT via image_fill_area (which would solid-fill the emblem to a black blob and destroy every counter) or image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image, no mask); image_remove_background is used only on the sample photo's outer felt ground (no enclosed-counter knockout is claimed anywhere); image_crop_and_resize only downscales the 3600x4500 sample to 1600x2000, never upscales or canvas-extends; no generative fill/expand, no upscaling, no text-to-image, no from-scratch art or font design. The agent performs NO measurement: it works by eye and reports the parameters it applied.
hardness_rationale: The FAILURE GATE is a set of CRAFT DECISIONS the agent can visibly get wrong, none requiring it to measure a pixel. (1) DIVERGENT PER-SHEET NEUTRALIZATION BY EYE: the six sheets carry six different casts and three different tilts; the agent must dial DIFFERENT straighten angles and DIFFERENT (often opposite-sign, and for the green/magenta frames a green-magenta rather than warm-cool) white-balance moves that all drive their in-frame 18% grey card to ONE shared neutral white - if it applies one global recipe (or per-frame auto-tone) the sheets clean to different whites, the marks binarize at different thresholds and trace at visibly different line weights, breaking the brief's 'one set, same visual weight' so the family looks drawn by different hands. (2) MASK-POLARITY DUAL TRACE ON THE CREST: a whole-raster trace that keeps fill and keyline as separate shapes (multi-level strike art) versus an emblem SELECTION fed to image_vectorize, which returns a single solid silhouette (the single-level strike master); swap the polarities and the detail art loses its keyline or the strike master arrives as un-cuttable two-shape art. (3) TRIAGE OF THE PHOTOGRAPHED SAMPLE COIN: it looks like a sixth coin design but is a photo of a struck 3D metal object with relief and sheen on felt and must be routed to image_remove_background for the packshot, NOT the tracer - feed it to image_vectorize like the flat sheets and it returns garbage relief/sheen paths, invisible until the SVG is opened. The HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS are cross-asset consistency across six deliberately mismatched sheets driven to one white point (each judged by eye and REPORTED as the parameters applied, so 'matched' is checkable) and constraint-reasoning around the tracer (selection->silhouette vs whole-raster multi-shape) and around the recolor limits (the family's black/white reproductions are properties of one vector master, and the gold/silver are AUTHORED metal proofs built from tone+tint+grain, because image_fill_area would blob the emblem and image_apply_color_overlay cannot mask). The deliberate TRAP is the brief's own tempting 'clean the sheets and vector every coin design': cleaning them the same way, or tracing the sample-coin photo, both look right and both fail, and both are invisible until the SVGs are inspected; a further trap is inventing a straighten on the three flat scans or copying the crest's balance onto the opposite-cast frames. The agent NEVER reads a pixel, hex or channel value: it neutralizes each grey card by eye and REPORTS the straighten angle and temperature/tint/exposure/whites it dialed per sheet - an applied-settings log, not a measurement. ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked, never a step the agent performs): neutrality is measured on the RETAINED card-bearing neutralized masters (steps 3/13/16/19/23/26, card still in frame) - all six grey cards must resolve to one common neutral white point with no residual cast and no clipped white; card-EXCLUSION is checked separately on the delivered cropped traces; the full-detail SVGs are distinguishable from the single-strike master by shape/path count; the two metal proofs read as struck relief (not flat swatches) and share one relief base; sample_packshot_web.jpg is a raster at exactly 1600x2000 sRGB with no vector paths; and the returned per-sheet parameters must be NON-identical across the six sheets while converging on the stated shared white point.
